en.caption: Outlands Oozes
rows: A yugoloth arms dealer has captured a hundred {@creature Gray Ooze||gray oozes} and seeks to sell them in the gate-town of Rigus as a weapon capable of destroying Acheron's floating cubes. A rival hires the characters to steal and dispose of the oozes.

Within a {@creature gelatinous cube} influenced by {@area Gehenna|02e|x} floats a gigantic fiendish skull. Numerous Fiends revere the cube and interpret depraved schemes and threatening orders from its quivering. A Celestial seeks aid in destroying the cube.
A bog in a region influenced by {@area Carceri|026|x} is swamped with countless {@creature Black Pudding||black puddings}. The characters are hired to recover a lost relic from the bottom of the bog.

A chef in the gate-town of {@book Tradegate|SatO|3|Tradegate} wants the characters to retrieve royal jelly from a hive of giant bees (use the {@creature giant wasp} stat block). He doesn't note that the hive's honey takes the form of sweet-tasting {@creature Ochre Jelly||ochre jellies}.

en.caption: Outlands Monstrosities
rows: The characters are hired to recover cargo from a crashed vessel brimming with rare technology, but the wreckage is overrun with {@creature Rust Monster||rust monsters}.

The characters have to retrieve a treasure from a group of mischievous {@creature Sprite||sprites}. The sprites are secretly defended by {@creature Mimic||mimics} influenced by {@area Elysium|02a|x} that take the form of tiny, whimsical cottages.
A pride of {@creature Displacer Beast||displacer beasts} stalks a band of traveling merchants. The merchants seek protection from the predators hunting them for sport.

A {@creature drider} influenced by {@area Arborea|015|x} runs a {@creature giant spider} ranch. She hires the characters to hunt a rare breed of {@creature sunfly|MPP} (detailed {@area later|07a|x} in this book) that, when fed to her spiders, will allow them to produce a remarkable type of silk.

en.caption: Outlands Aberrations
rows: An {@creature aboleth} travels in a muck-filled, orbicular carriage, seeking to better understand the Outer Planes in preparation for a future world-domination scheme.

A {@creature beholder} influenced by {@area the Abyss|00b|x} has compound eyes and looks like a floating, cyclopean fly head. It promises not to destroy the characters if they bring it a corpse it has never tasted before.
A dejected {@creature red slaad} wishes to be reunited with its {@creature slaad tadpole}, but it isn't certain where—or in what—it implanted its egg.
A hirsute, axe-wielding {@creature flumph} influenced by {@area Ysgard|04d|x} quests across the land, seeking legendary beasts to slay and epic songs to sing.

en.caption: Outlands Celestials
rows: An {@creature empyrean} calls for aid in taking back a corner of the Outlands overrun by demons.
Wearing grim armor and displaying a rust-colored horn, a {@creature unicorn} influenced by {@area Acheron|010|x} challenges all it encounters to mortal combat.

A fallen {@creature deva}, now neutral aligned, is on permanent vacation. The mellow angel is a font of multiversal secrets, but it shares them only with strangers who prove themselves more relaxed than it.

A {@creature couatl} influenced by {@area Limbo|038|x} has color-changing wings and insists passersby convince it that they're worthy of existing. If the couatl isn't convinced, it has a 50 percent chance of either attacking or wandering off.

en.caption: Outlands Elementals
rows: {@creature Water Elemental||Water elementals} travel in a group that looks like a long, wandering river.
Some skull-headed {@creature Azer||azers} have been influenced by {@area the Nine Hells|045|x}. They escort a heavily armored caravan of rare ore to the gate-town of Ribcage.
A wounded {@creature mud mephit} asks the characters to help it deliver a sealed package to a leader in a nearby gate-town.

A wealthy {@creature dao} that glistens with gemstones has been influenced by {@area Arborea|015|x}. It leads a parade of glimmering {@creature galeb duhr} between gate-towns as part of a shopping spree for precious rocks.

en.caption: Outlands Fey
rows: Revelers joined a group of {@creature Satyr||satyrs} in their festivities. As the satyrs' celebration has continued for over a year, the revelers seek the characters' help in extricating themselves without offending their hosts.
A kindly {@creature green hag} influenced by {@area Elysium|02a|x} invites passersby to join her for tea in her cottage made of sweets. She makes some of the best cookies in the Outlands.

A pack of {@creature Blink Dog||blink dogs} tracks a band of {@creature Maelephant|MPP|maelephants} (presented {@area later|074|x} in this book) to prevent them from spoiling lands influenced by the Upper Planes.
A gnarled {@creature dryad} influenced by {@area Carceri|026|x} seeks to entrap creatures within the root-snarled, prison-like cavern beneath her grove.

A hero requests the characters' help in gaining the aid of a legendary steed called a nic'epona, a {@creature nightmare} influenced by one of the Upper Planes.
Rival {@creature Incubus||incubi} seek to recruit the characters to serve either a {@creature balor} warlord or a {@creature pit fiend} general whose fiendish armies are prepared to clash nearby.

en.caption: Outlands Plants
rows: A young {@creature treant} wants to put down roots. It asks the characters to help it travel around the Outlands so it can find a suitable place to call home.

A {@creature myconid sovereign} has convinced a group of {@creature Githzerai Monk||githzerai monks} to abandon their teachings and follow its path to serenity. Another githzerai hires the characters to oust the fungal guru.
An herbalist has cultivated a unique breed of {@creature Gas Spore||gas spores}. She hires the characters to convey the spores to her buyer without setting off the fungi.

A resident of the gate-town of {@book Ecstasy|SatO|3|Ecstasy} is missing. His garden of {@creature Twig Blight||twig blights}—influenced by {@area Elysium|02a|x} to resemble topiary sculptures—haven't been fed and now sow chaos in town.

A {@creature triceratops} influenced by {@area Mechanus|03d|x} and composed of simple geometric shapes charges creatures that enter the angular canyons it inhabits. It moves only in straight lines and turns only at right angles.
{@creature Stirge||Stirges} drawn from countless worlds congregate in a tornado-sized, bloodsucking cloud that threatens a gate-town.
A desiccated {@creature giant frog} influenced by {@area Pandemonium|049|x} screams whenever it opens its mouth. Its interior is even noisier.

en.caption: Outlands Undead
rows: The characters find a trapped {@creature crawling claw}. Rather than attacking, the severed hand can lead the characters to the thankful immortal who lost it.

A {@creature banshee} influenced by {@area Acheron|010|x} appears as a fallen knight-commander with a legion of {@creature Specter||specters}. Guardians of the gate-town of Rigus hire the characters to help banish the phantom army.

A {@creature lich} seeks to dominate the gate-town of Hopeless and see it dragged into Hades with himself as its ruler. Citizens of the gate-town entreat the characters to keep the gate-town hopeful enough that it doesn't fall into the Lower Plane.
Several confused {@creature ghost} {@area petitioners|004|x} have become lost. They seek someone to pass judgment on their lives and deliver them to the proper planes.

en.caption: Outlands Humanoids
rows: The characters need to find a wandering {@creature priest} who alone knows the ritual necessary to open a specific portal.
Several gnome {@creature Mage||mages} seek help recovering their walking castle from a band of aggressive, spine-covered {@creature lizardfolk} influenced by {@area the Abyss|00b|x}.
The characters stumble across a youthful or elderly {@creature commoner} who doesn't know how they came to be in the Outlands and who wants only to go home.

A {@creature bandit captain} and his gang seek the characters' help as they plan a heist in the realm of an immortal being, like the {@book Realm of the Norns|SatO|3|Realm of the Norns} or {@book Wonderhome|SatO|3|Wonderhome} (see {@book Sigil and the Outlands|SatO} for details on both locations).

A beautiful but vain {@creature flesh golem} influenced by {@area Arborea|015|x} insists on following a character until the character sketches, sculpts, or otherwise artistically renders it.

A gang of inquisitive {@creature Monodrone||monodrones} and its {@creature duodrone} leader insist on following a character, saying they expect that individual's doom to be "statistically noteworthy."
A {@creature clay golem} influenced by {@area the Beastlands|01d|x} has been transformed into the walking hive that's home to numerous {@creature Swarm of Wasps||swarms of insects (wasps)}.

Nobody is as smart as me, and I need to prove that all the time.

I'm a bully who backs down when faced with any sort of resistance.
Every problem can be solved with the use of force.

en.caption: Devil Bonds
rows: I and my comrades fought well in the Blood War, and our service demands respect.
Evil without law is a pointless exercise in destruction. Rules make us what we are.
Those who follow me rely on my wisdom to ensure their prosperity.
One day I will have revenge on those who defied me.
If I do my duty, in time I will be rewarded.
We don't corrupt mortals. We teach them enlightened self-interest.

"I periodically slip into a catatonic state, staring off into the distance for long stretches at a time."
"I see an altered version of reality, with my mind convincing itself that things are true even in the face of overwhelming evidence to the contrary."
"My mind is slipping away, and my intelligence seems to wax and wane."
"I am constantly scratching at unseen fungal infections."

en.caption: Githzerai Personality Traits
rows: All energy must be expended to a useful end. Frivolity is the first step to defeat.
Patience in all things. The first step in any venture is the most treacherous.
Emotions are a trap, meant to weaken the intellect and disturb the nerves. Pay them no heed.
Begin only those tasks you will finish. Strike only that which you will kill.

You prefer to hide during a fight.
There is no difference between what you think and what you say.

en.caption: Duergar Adventurer Story Hooks
rows: You are a heretic, drawn to worship of Moradin.
Caught stealing, you escaped imprisonment but not before torture left you with a scar or lasting injury.
You were enslaved by drow or mind flayers but escaped to the surface.
You seek only to test yourself in battle with monsters.
Profit is all that matters to you.
The best way to defeat the folk of the surface is to study them firsthand.
en.name: Duergar Adventurer Story Hooks

en.caption: Cult Organization
rows: Conspiracy. Members use passwords and double-blind communication.
False Front. The cult puts on an elaborate deception to appear as a harmless civic group.
Criminal Enterprise. The cult is organized through a thieves' guild.
Network. The cult has a secret alliance of members who have infiltrated the lower ranks of every organization of note in the region.
Cult of Personality. The cult leader is a beloved figure renowned for great, benevolent deeds.
Entrenched. The cult is part of the local culture, a tradition that established decades ago and kept secret from outsiders.

en.caption: Duergar Quirks
rows: A separate personality in your mind provides advice and guidance to you.
Your gear must be perfectly arranged, otherwise someone must bleed.
When there isn't a roof over your head, you keep your eyes on the ground.
You don't talk unless you absolutely must.
The outside world is a giant cave, and nothing will convince you otherwise.
Humans fascinate you, and you collect odd trinkets of their culture.
en.name: Duergar Quirks

en.caption: Madness of Fraz-Urb'luu
rows: "I never let anyone know the truth about my actions or intentions, even if doing so would be beneficial to me."
"I have intermittent hallucinations and fits of catatonia."
"My mind wanders as I have elaborate fantasies that have no bearing on reality. When I return my focus to the world, I have a hard time remembering that it was just a daydream."
"I convince myself that things are true, even in the face of overwhelming evidence to the contrary."
"My perception of reality doesn't match anyone else's. It makes me prone to violent delusions that make no sense to anyone else."
en.name: Madness of Fraz-Urb'luu

en.caption: Githzerai Flaws
rows: I see githyanki machinations behind every threat.
I believe in the supremacy of the gith and that githzerai and githyanki will align to rule the multiverse.
I respond to even minor threats with overwhelming displays of force.
The next time I laugh will be the first. The sound of merriment takes me to the edge of violence.

en.caption: Devil Flaws
rows: My frustration boils over into violence.
I obey the law, but I strain at its limits to the point of heresy.
I put the minimum effort possible into anything that isn't my own idea.
A low profile is the best defense of all.
I'm so reliant on the laws of the Nine Hells that I panic without their guidance.
I am secretly jealous of the freedom that mortals enjoy.

en.caption: Reasons for Adventuring
rows: Peeling taters and herding goats all the time wasn't your cup of tea.
You fell asleep on a raft one day and woke up near a human city. You were so thrilled with the strange sights and tasty food that you never turned back.
What started off as simple pumpkin pillaging from nearby farms turned into your becoming a wandering rogue for hire.
You talked to a nice faerie in the woods, and all of a sudden you were a thousand miles from home.
Your village elder told you so many stories about being a rogue in an adventuring party that you couldn't resist the urge to try doing it yourself.
A friend dared you to jump on the back of a sleeping horse, which turned out to be a pegasus, and your life hasn't slowed down since.
en.name: Reasons for Adventuring
